blocks.text: Choose whether a quantity threshold includes its boundary.
Use == to test equality and != to test inequality.
< and > test strict ordering. <= and >= also include equality.

At the boundary, >= includes equality but > does not. Use == for an equality test, not assignment’s =.

blocks.text: Combine quantity and budget conditions.
For boolean conditions, and is true when both are true; or is true when at least one is true; not reverses the truth value.
and skips its second operand if the first is false. or skips its second operand if the first is true.
not has higher priority than and, and and higher priority than or. Parentheses make grouping explicit.

blocks.code:
quantity_ok = 3 >= 3
budget_ok = 12 >= 15
print(quantity_ok and budget_ok)
print(quantity_ok or budget_ok)
print(not budget_ok)
print(not (quantity_ok and budget_ok))

annotations.text: quantity_ok is True, so and evaluates budget_ok; the result is False.
quantity_ok is True, so or skips budget_ok; the result is True.
Trace grouping and whether the second operand is evaluated.
Parentheses group quantity_ok and budget_ok; not reverses that grouped result.

blocks.text: Track quantity_ok and budget_ok separately before combining them. Mark whether a second operand is needed, then read any not and parentheses before evaluating the full rule.

blocks.text: Convert numeric quantity text before using it in a calculation.
int(value) constructs an integer from suitable numeric text or a number. A float-to-int conversion truncates toward zero.
float(text) constructs a floating-point value from supported numeric text.
str(value) constructs a string representation.
Invalid numeric text can raise ValueError: the value is unsuitable for that conversion.
Assign the converted result to a name for later calculations. The original name changes only if it is the assignment target.

blocks.code:
quantity_text = "3"
quantity = float(quantity_text)
price = float("4.5")
price = quantity * price
print(quantity_text)
print(quantity)
print(price)
print(int(-3.8))

annotations.text: Bind quantity to the converted float; quantity_text remains text.
Use the current quantity and price, then rebind price to the product.

blocks.text: Keep quantity_text separate from the converted quantity. The price conversion supplies a numeric value for multiplication. Compare suitable numeric text with an arbitrary word, and read float-to-int conversion as truncation toward zero.
A conversion returns a value; it does not automatically rebind quantity_text. Truncating toward zero is not general rounding.

public.prompt: Which statement correctly describes int(-3.8), str(3), and float("three")?

a.message: int(-3.8) truncates toward zero to -3; str(3) constructs the string "3"; unsuitable numeric text "three" makes float raise ValueError.

b.message: int(-3.8) truncates toward zero, not down to -4. str(3) produces a string, not an integer, and "three" is unsuitable numeric text, so float raises ValueError.

c.message: The integer truncation and string construction are correct, but float("three") raises ValueError rather than returning 0.0.
